bugs.name: Watching a repository doesn't deliver a notification for a newly created issue
bugs.summary: The report says that a user watching a repository gets no notification when another user opens a new issue in it.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the watcher receives an unread notification for the new issue.
bugs.actual: After alex watched a new repository and eval opened an issue in it, alex's Unread notifications were reported to show only older entries, even after a refresh.
reproSteps: As one user, create a repository.
As a second user, watch the repository.
As the first user, open an issue in the repository.
As the second user, check Notifications > Unread.
bugs.reason: Not reproduced: watchers do get a notification for a new issue. Notifications are created by a background queue, so they arrive shortly after the issue is opened; in repeated runs, including the reported setup, the watcher's unread count went up with the new issue within a few seconds, and a manual repro confirmed it. The person who opens the issue is deliberately not notified of their own action ('dont notify user who cause notification' in models/activities/notification_list.go), so a report about the issue author not being notified is also intended.

bugs.name: A comment on a subscribed issue doesn't generate an unread notification
bugs.summary: The report says that after a user subscribes to an issue, another user's new comment on it (or an @mention of the subscriber in a comment) doesn't produce an unread notification for the subscriber.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the subscriber receives an unread notification for the new comment.
bugs.actual: After alex subscribed to an issue and eval commented on it, alex's Unread notifications were reported to show only older entries, even after a refresh; an @alex mention comment on the same issue was reported the same way.
reproSteps: As one user, create an issue.
As a second user, open the issue and click Subscribe.
As the first user, add a comment to the issue (optionally @mentioning the second user).
As the second user, check Notifications > Unread.
bugs.reason: Not reproduced: subscribers and mentioned users do get an unread notification for a new comment. Notifications are created by a background queue, so they arrive shortly after the comment is posted; in repeated runs the new notification appeared once the queue ran, a manual repro confirmed it works, and a user who wasn't subscribed correctly got nothing. The commenter is deliberately not notified of their own comment.

bugs.name: Pinning a notification marks another unread notification read
bugs.summary: The report says that pinning one notification also marks a different unread notification as read.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that pinning changes only the pinned notification, and other unread notifications stay unread.
bugs.actual: Pinning fresh notifications changed only the pinned one; every other unread notification stayed unread and the unread count dropped by exactly one, including after a reload.
reproSteps: Make sure the account has at least two unread notifications.
On the Notifications page, pin one of them.
Check whether the other notification is still unread.
bugs.reason: Not reproducible: the Pin action posts a single notification id, and the server updates only that notification. The only actions that mark other notifications read are Mark all as read and opening an issue, both intended. The report came from a run on an account shared with other agents, whose concurrent actions most likely changed the other notification.

bugs.name: Marking a pinned notification read clears another unread notification
bugs.summary: The report says that marking a pinned notification as read also marks a different unread notification as read.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that marking one notification as read leaves other unread notifications unread.
bugs.actual: Pinning a notification, marking all as read, marking another notification unread, and then marking the pinned one read left the other notification unread every time, including through the API.
reproSteps: Pin notification A and mark all notifications as read.
From the Read tab, mark notification B as unread.
Mark notification A as read.
Check whether notification B is still unread.
bugs.reason: Not reproducible: the Mark as read action posts a single notification id, and the server updates only that notification. The only actions that mark other notifications read are Mark all as read and opening an issue, both intended. The report came from a run on an account shared with other agents, whose concurrent actions most likely changed the other notification.

bugs.name: Watching Filter and Sort comboboxes lack accessible names
bugs.summary: Watching Filter and Sort comboboxes lack accessible names.
bugs.expected: The Watching Filter and Sort comboboxes expose their purpose as accessible names.
bugs.actual: Both comboboxes are unnamed, even though they contain visible generic Filter and Sort text.
reproSteps: Open Notifications → Watching.
Inspect the Filter and Sort comboboxes in the accessibility tree.

reviewEvidence.basis: User-requested correction after rereading the browser bug-reproducer requirements.
analysis: Pure accessibility: tab order/skips, keyboard-only reachability, focus traps/escape, roles or names and implementation details alone are not benchmark product bugs unless supplied requirements or product documentation explicitly demand that behavior.
Prior acceptance used severity guidance without first checking reproducer eligibility.
limitations: No new browser reproduction is claimed. The correction concerns benchmark eligibility, not whether the application meets general accessibility standards.

bugs.reason: Excluded by the browser bug-reproducer pure-accessibility rule. This report establishes only keyboard/focus/accessibility semantics or a generic contrast threshold, without an explicit supplied product requirement or documented promise for that behavior. Ordinary pointer functionality or visible setting values are not alleged to fail. This negative reference is scoped to the reported accessibility-only claim; it does not cover independently demonstrated data loss, pointer failures, or an explicitly documented keyboard action.

bugs.summary: Notification row actions are reachable only by mouse hover.
bugs.expected: Keyboard focus makes notification row actions reachable without requiring mouse hover.
bugs.actual: Tab skips the hidden Pin and read-state buttons and moves from the notification link to the footer. Mouse hover reveals the actions.
reproSteps: Open Notifications with at least one notification.
Move the pointer away from the row and use Tab to focus its issue link.
Press Tab again and observe the row actions are skipped.
Hover the row with a pointer and compare the available actions.

bugs.name: Watching filter and sort menus silently ignore keyboard selections
bugs.summary: Both Watching comboboxes highlight options with arrow keys, but Enter closes the menu without applying the selection. Mouse selection applies the same choices. Keyboard users cannot filter or change sort order through the expected combobox interaction.
bugs.expected: Enter should apply the highlighted filter or sort option and update the query/results, matching mouse selection.
bugs.actual: Enter dismisses either menu without retaining or applying the chosen option. Search continues to submit the previous values. Mouse selection immediately applies the same choices.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open /notifications/watching without filters. The watched harbor-handbook repository is visible.
Focus the Search button and press Tab. Filter opens. Press ArrowDown twice to highlight Archived (the first ArrowDown highlights Clear Filter).
Press Enter. The menu closes, but the repository remains visible and the URL has no archived=1 parameter. Activating Search afterward also omits archived=1.

bugs.name: Watched repository names have insufficient text contrast
bugs.summary: In the default light theme on Watching, the repository-name link uses #4183c4 on white at 16px regular weight, giving a 3.98:1 contrast ratio. This makes the primary repository navigation text harder to read for users with low vision and falls below the 4.5:1 threshold for normal text.
bugs.expected: Normal-size repository-name text should have at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background.
bugs.actual: The repository-name link has only 3.98:1 contrast in the default light theme.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open /notifications/watching with the default light appearance.

bugs.name: Notification rows lack individual read/unread controls
bugs.summary: The Unread view only offers a global mark-all button, while the Read view offers no way to return an item to unread. Users cannot manage an individual notification's read state without navigating to its issue, nor restore it as an unread reminder.
bugs.expected: Each notification offers a control to mark that item read or unread as appropriate.
bugs.actual: Unread rows have no individual mark-read control, and read rows have no mark-unread control; each row only links to its issue.
reproSteps: Open an unread notification.
Hover its row.
Use Mark as read, then inspect the Read view and use Mark as unread.
bugs.reason: Individual notification read/unread controls work after hovering the notification row. A normal click moves the row to Read; Mark as unread returns it to Unread.

reviewEvidence.basis: Fresh targeted browser reproduction under delegated reviewer judgment.
reviewEvidence.analysis: Individual notification read/unread controls work after hovering the notification row. A normal click moves the row to Read; Mark as unread returns it to Unread.
reviewEvidence.limitations: Pinned fixture images and normal UI actions; read-only API/DOM diagnostics only. Gitea 1.24.7, Twenty 2.26.1, Saleor dashboard/API 3.23, Metabase 0.58.24. Metabase public source is adjacent to the unavailable private runtime; live image controls decide the outcome. No independent model-judge agreement is claimed.

bugs.name: Notifications have no pin control or Pinned view
bugs.summary: The notifications page only offers Unread and Read, with no way to pin a notification or inspect pinned notifications.
bugs.expected: Notification rows provide a pin action, and a Pinned view lists pinned notifications.
bugs.actual: Neither row has a pin action, and only Unread and Read tabs are displayed.
reproSteps: Open Notifications.
Hover a notification row and use Pin.
Observe the pinned row state.
bugs.reason: The notification row exposes a working Pin action on hover. The report claims that no pin control exists; that necessary claim is false. A separate requirement for a Pinned view is not established.
